_doc: Headwaters source registry - PLATFORM-SCOPE families (P5-6). Datasets used by every city, registered once here instead of duplicated per city. Only families that actually VERSION belong here: OpenStreetMap and Google Dynamic World are continuously updated with no editions, so they stay in the coverage allowlist as a freshness question (P5-1), not an edition watch. Schema + design notes: docs/specs/headwaters.md (local).

sources.publisher: Fathom / University of Bristol (Hawker et al.)
sources.notes: FABDEM V1-2 - satellite DEM with buildings and forests removed - underpins the elevation-band layer in all five cities, honest at ~30 m horizontal / ~2 m vertical. A new FABDEM version changes every band boundary at once, which is exactly why this is registered once at platform scope rather than five times. LICENCE FLAG: FABDEM is CC BY-NC-SA, non-commercial - relevant if any BRSR or commercial track ever reuses these layers. The canonical data host is data.bris.ac.uk but its dataset paths need an exact opaque id we do not have; the Fathom product page is the stable, verified surface (200 on 2026-07-26).

sources.license: HydroSHEDS licence (free for non-commercial and most uses, attribution required)
sources.notes: HydroBASINS/HydroRIVERS is the skeleton under every cascade reconstruction (Chennai 755 nodes, Bengaluru 1,033, plus Madurai and Mumbai) and under the Chennai sub-basin climate-risk clip (hybas_12 + state clip). A version bump would move cascade topology everywhere at once - a platform-wide SCHEMA-BREAK candidate, not a routine roll-forward. page-hash may be noisy on a marketing-styled page; tighten with a selector if it false-positives.

JRC Global Surface Water v1.4 supplies the long-run water-extent trend in every rich-body deep-zoom panel across the 20-body cohort. A new JRC version re-bases those trends, so it is a review event rather than an auto-apply. dependsOn points at the rich-bodies GROUP - the coverage gate collapses that directory to one logical artifact rather than 129 folders.

Google Open Buildings v3 is one of the two independent building-footprint sources in the rich-body encroachment verification; Overture is the other, and the artifacts deliberately compare them side by side. A version bump on either changes the verification result, which is why both are registered.

Overture ships MONTHLY, the fastest cadence of any platform family, and a workflow already re-pulls it on the 8th - so this entry is about knowing the release landed, not about triggering the fetch. GAP FOUND 2026-07-26: our overture artifacts record only computed_at, NOT the Overture release version they were built from, so we cannot currently tell which release a given rich-body panel reflects. Worth adding to the ingest script. docs.overturemaps.org/release/ 404s and the GitHub releases API returns an empty list, so overturemaps.org/download is the watchable surface.
